Overview

FY26 results demonstrate a good performance, in line with the Group’s guidance, following notable growth in the second half of the year. The Value Delivery Plan (VDP) is being executed well, delivering benefits earlier than planned, which coupled with growth initiatives and innovation provide an increasingly positive outlook for YouGov. The extension of the Group’s debt facilities has been completed, and a share buyback launching today. The Shopper strategic review is ongoing, with further updates to be provided in due course. The Group is confident in the delivery of adjusted operating profit growth for FY27 of between 7% and 12%, in line with current market expectations.

About YouGov 

YouGov is a global research data and analytics group. Our mission is to offer unparalleled insight into what the world really thinks and does. With operations in the Americas, UK, Mainland Europe and Asia Pacific, we have one of the world’s largest research networks. 

Above all, YouGov is powered by reality. That stems from a unique panel of 31 million of registered members across 64 markets and millions of interconnected data points. Our unique approach to recruiting and engaging with our panel, combined with our state-of-the-art technology platforms, enables us to deliver real-world, real-time insights that lead to better decision-making and a competitive advantage for our clients. 

As innovators and pioneers of online market research, we have a strong reputation as a trusted source of accurate data and insights. Testament to this, YouGov data is regularly referenced by the global press, and we are consistently one of the most quoted market research sources in the world.

Chair’s Statement

Introduction and overview

I am pleased to report on a year of substantial progress across the breadth of YouGov. Having developed a clear transformation agenda, Stephan and the team are reinventing our offer to customers and positioning YouGov to deliver sustainable growth through FY27 and beyond.

The macro-environment in which we operate in is changing faster than at any time in recent history. Technological advances mean that how we work has to evolve, what we work on is different and our offer to our customers needs to be reimagined. Understanding both the opportunity and the risks associated with AI goes to the heart of our strategic thinking.

Underpinning the business that Stephan has created at YouGov is an incredible asset, and that is our data. YouGov has unique proprietary data assets which we believe will play a crucial, and value-creating role in the AI-led transformation of our industry. It is the untapped value-creating potential in our data, especially in an AI world, which appealed when I was asked to join the Board last September and the quality of the asset reassured me when I stepped up to Chair in February.

YouGov in Three Years – a clear sense of direction

Our vision is for YouGov to be the world’s leading provider of opinion and behavioural data. Understanding the vision, what it means, how it gets executed, the necessary skills, capabilities and risks are the agenda for every Board meeting. 

In June 2026, the Board welcomed members of senior management, clients and industry experts to join our annual strategy session. At this session, we explored the vision of YouGov in three years both from a commercial perspective, meeting the changing needs and expectations of our clients, and from a technology perspective, considering the tools and resources we need to optimise our existing product suite and innovate the products of the future. From this session and many other such Board interactions over the last year, it is clear to us that YouGov’s transformation will result in a more efficient, effective, market-leading data business. 

The business will also need to continuously develop new products and enhance existing ones to continue to meet client needs. At the same time we need to look at all opportunities to embed efficiencies unlocked by AI throughout our business. We are addressing this in a systematic way in our Value Delivery Plan (VDP). 

Together, this means the Board and Executive team are focussed on realising the underlying value and long-term potential of our assets. 

We are encouraged by progress in our Data Products division and the resilience of our Research business. In March, the Board launched a strategic review of the Shopper division. The strategic rationale for the acquisition remains unchanged, and the review is ongoing. We continue to evaluate opportunities to maximise shareholder value while supporting the Group's long-term strategic objectives, and we will provide a further update in due course. 

Board and leadership change

Since taking the Chairmanship, and in light of the strategic change we are going through, my priority has been to ensure we have the right skills, capabilities and experience around both the Board and the Senior Management team.

We announced the appointment of Wayne Levings as CEO in August, joining the business in November 2026 initially as CEO-elect, to then step up to CEO and join the Board no later than February 2027. This transition enables a smooth handover from Stephan to Wayne. Wayne brings extensive industry expertise and his skills in transformation and operational excellence will help to drive our progress and value creation. 

We are delighted that Stephan, following the CEO handover, will move into a non-executive role on the Board with the additional responsibility of chairing our newly formed Innovation Committee. Keeping Stephan’s unrivalled depth of expertise, in our sector and what makes us unique, is clearly in the best interests of YouGov and retaining those skills around the Board table will enhance our ability to create a more exciting business in the future. I would also like to thank Stephan for stepping back into the CEO role nearly two years ago. Stephan returned with the aim to restore stability, build momentum, in our new products and set a new direction for the business and he has delivered on all those commitments.

As well as the CEO role, we have to ensure we have the right skills and capabilities in the other positions around the boardroom. We need to ensure the Board understands the changing needs of our business, its strategy and the broader market context in which we operate. In practice, this means our Directors regularly meet with Stephan and the team above and beyond attending formal meetings. Recognising the complexity of the business, it also means we need a diverse mix of skills, capabilities and talent to deliver YouGov’s ambition. We have conducted an extensive review of the skills and experience we currently have in comparison to what we will need in the future to successfully support and challenge, in equal measure, the Executive team in the execution of our strategic objectives. As a result of this review, through rotation and succession planning, we anticipate appointing two Non-Executive Directors during FY27 to ensure orderly transition for the Audit & Risk Committee as Ashley Martin completes his nine-year term, and to further deepen our AI product and technology expertise. We will announce developments in our succession planning in due course. 

There has been significant change around the Board this year. I recognise the role played by my predecessor Deborah Davis and thank her for her leadership of the Board for the first half of the year. I would also like to thank Shalini Govil-Pai who left the Board in March following the end of her three-year term. Andrea Newman has served on the Board of YouGov for almost nine years and will not stand for re-election at the upcoming AGM. In Executive Leadership changes, Alex McIntosh stepped down as Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and from the Board in February, after almost 20 years with YouGov. James Davies was appointed as Chief Financial Officer initially on an interim basis and does not serve on the Board at this time. I wish to thank Alex and all our departing Directors for their contribution, insight, commitment and guidance during their tenures. 

Our sustainable business 

YouGov’s business is underpinned by an ethos of transparency and trust, and a desire to give the world a voice. Sustainability and ESG considerations are embedded throughout our business model and values. Our ESG strategy, which champions sustainable, ethical and responsible business practices across every aspect of our operations, helps safeguard YouGov’s reputation, culture, commitment to opinion neutrality, and ability to deliver social value to our communities while contributing to sustainable growth. This approach is well established, and our ESG report, included within the Annual Report, highlights our progress during the year, with extensive additional information available on our website.

Capital allocation

Since 2012, the Board has adopted a progressive dividend policy. However, the Board believes that there is a disconnect between the prevailing share price and our view of the Company’s intrinsic value, and as a result the Board has re-evaluated its distribution policy for this year. 

As we have previously announced, the Company will be replacing the dividend for FY26 and are pleased to confirm a share buyback of up to £15m (the "Share Buyback Programme"), to commence as soon as possible. Further details will be announced separately. 

The Board believes that an updated distribution policy, introducing flexibility into the form of distribution between dividend and share buyback, supports a more efficient use of capital and we will keep the distribution policy under consideration for the FY27 financial year.

Looking ahead 

I wish to take a moment to thank the Executive Leadership team and wider workforce on behalf of the Board for how they are embracing our transformation. Working in new ways accelerates cultural change and it is the Board’s role to ensure we uphold our values – be fast, be fearless, get it right, respect and trust – to preserve what makes YouGov unique while developing the new skills and capabilities to drive us forward. Stephan and the Board are confident in our direction of travel and believe this will transform the business, realise YouGov’s vision and deliver long-term value to stakeholders.

Chief Executive Officer’s Statement

In February 2025, I returned to the role of YouGov’s Chief Executive Officer on an interim basis. At the time of my return, my objective was clear and I laid out three main priorities: to stabilise the business, rebuild momentum in innovation, and ensure a smooth leadership transition that would position YouGov for its next phase of growth. Looking back on FY26, I believe we have made meaningful progress against all three priorities.

The past year has been characterised by continued macro-economic volatility and rapid advances in the implementation of Artificial Intelligence. Against a backdrop of geopolitical instability, organisations remained focussed on cost discipline. At the same time, investment increasingly shifted towards AI infrastructure capable of delivering higher productivity and returns. Within the market research industry, this has led to the growing importance of trusted data in an AI-driven world, creating a significant opportunity for YouGov.

Our ambition remains to become the universal infrastructure for trusted opinion and behavioural data sharing. We believe our proprietary panel, rich connected dataset and trusted brand place us in a unique position to help clients combine the power of AI with high-quality human data.

FY26: Continued progress on key priorities

Our first priority was to stabilise performance by accelerating revenue growth and strengthening cost discipline. During the year, we maintained a measured approach to headcount expansion, refreshed the Leadership team, and concentrated investment on initiatives that support revenue generation, client value and long-term growth.

The renewed focus on our core strengths has enabled our Data Products business to deliver encouraging growth, supported by continued client demand for our high-quality daily brand tracking solution. Our Research division accelerated its growth as demand for strategic research projects continued. As outlined last year, the Shopper division is undergoing a period of targeted investment to strengthen its offering, support client retention and position it to capture new growth opportunities over the medium term. 

More broadly, FY26 was a year of investment and the start of a significant transformation programme designed to strengthen our foundations for future growth. A key element of this transformation is our Value Delivery Plan (VDP), a multi-phase programme focussed on improving efficiency, simplifying operations and creating new revenue opportunities. 

Having stabilised the business, our next focus was to increase momentum in product innovation to take advantage of the new opportunities presented by the rise of AI tools and capabilities. During FY26, we accelerated our efforts to enhance our user interfaces, add new feature sets and introduce AI across our products. In February 2026, we successfully launched YouGov Voices, an AI-powered interviewing tool enabling clients to collect rich, qualitative context from our panellists. As an add-on to YouGov BrandIndex, the product has helped secure several sales, including a $2m contract with a major professional services company. Early commercial success highlights growing demand for AI-enabled research solutions. In H2 FY26, we also introduced support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) standard across our products, enabling AI applications and agent environments to query our data using natural language. 

Our focus on AI extends beyond product innovation and into the way we operate as a business. During the year, we made significant progress on our research automation programme, one of the largest transformation initiatives underway at YouGov. We developed and began testing automated workflows designed to streamline the delivery of low-complexity research projects, reducing manual effort while improving consistency and scalability. This work brings together advances in AI, data science and our platform capabilities, and represents an important step towards a more efficient operating model that will enable our teams to focus more of their time on delivering value to clients.

The final priority has been to ensure a smooth and successful leadership transition. I am delighted to welcome Wayne Levings as CEO-elect next month and look forward to working closely with him to ensure an orderly and effective handover. I am confident that the actions we have taken to stabilise performance and strengthen the organisation mean that YouGov is stronger today than when I returned as CEO and that Wayne will inherit a business that is well positioned to capitalise on the significant opportunities ahead.

FY27 and beyond: Our Strategy

Our strategy goes beyond delivering leading market research and data analytics to our clients. It reflects a strategic shift towards embedding YouGov’s data directly into client workflows, platforms and AI-powered systems.

Over two decades, YouGov has built a strong foundation: a global proprietary panel, an automated data collection engine and a strong brand reputation. These competitive advantages are difficult to replicate and form the basis of our scalable, infrastructure-like model in this new age of AI.

Looking ahead, we will continue to progress our strategy across our four strategic pillars:

Next-Generation Panel Ecosystem

We strengthened the foundations of our panel ecosystem through the expansion of our ID-verified panel, the introduction of passive receipt data collection, and further enhancements to our fraud detection capabilities. During the year, we also conducted a review of our panel operations, established a clear set of operating principles, and launched initiatives to improve acquisition and retention while increasing the efficiency of third-party sample spend.

Looking ahead, we will build on these foundations by redesigning our value exchange with panellists, treat panel acquisition as a strategic growth lever and improve the recruitment flow. This will enhance data quality, improve unit economics and strengthen our long-term competitive advantage, supporting revenue growth acceleration and margin improvement.

AI-Powered Platform Transformation

Alongside progress in innovation and product development, we are advancing plans for a unified customer platform. This platform will expand functionality, simplify the client experience and provide a scalable foundation for future product integration.

In addition, we have launched YouGov Parallax, our latest innovation combining the power of digital twins with validation from real people. Following the release of our public prototype, we have received encouraging levels of client engagement and early commercial interest ahead of full launch.

Together, these initiatives represent important milestones in our evolution towards an AI-powered data and insights company, enabling us to deliver greater value to clients while accelerating innovation across the Group.

Focussed Growth and Portfolio Optimisation

We continued to sharpen our commercial focus through a range of targeted initiatives designed to simplify our portfolio, improve resource allocation and prioritise the sectors, products and regions most closely aligned with our long-term growth ambitions.

To accelerate progress in FY27, our commercial leadership will work closely with our Marketing, Product and Technology teams to develop and execute a global commercial strategy centred on our data and platform proposition. Additionally, our recent client wins give us confidence that we can continue to expand share of wallet with both new and existing multinational clients through our connected research solutions. 

The initiatives are intended to increase speed of new customer acquisition and average contract value.

Operational Efficiency and Simplification

Through the execution of our VDP, we have made continued progress on simplifying the organisation and reducing support function costs, and are developing plans to consolidate our systems. This ongoing efficiency drive is designed to increase accountability, reduce complexity and enable faster decision-making.

Chief Financial Officer’s Review

The Group delivered performance in line with the guidance provided at the H1 results in March for the 12 months ended 31 July 2026. FY26 has been another year of innovation although FY26 has also seen the launch of a material transformation programme. The CEO statement has gone into detail explaining how innovation has continued to be such an integral part of our journey and purpose. Investment has continued to ensure we remain at the forefront of our sector. The Value Delivery Plan (VDP) initiated in March, and discussed at our H1 results, covers a number of themes around the way we deliver for our clients, how we simplify our business and optimise the use of technology.

Group revenue was up 2% in reported and underlying1 terms to £396.6m during the period, reflecting growth across all divisions. Performance across the regions was mixed, with robust growth in the Americas of 6% on an underlying¹ basis and 1% growth in the UK. Mainland Europe recorded an underlying¹ decline of 1% due to the Shopper division, while Asia-Pacific was down 1%. In the context of a challenging market environment, the Group is encouraged by its resilient performance in line with the market and ahead of some of our closest peers.

Gross margin remained stable at 82% for the period. Group operating costs (excluding separately reported items) increased by 4% in reported terms to £268.9m (FY25: £258.9m). 

Adjusted operating profit1 decreased 11% to £54.3m (FY25: £60.7m), primarily reflecting increased investment in growth initiatives within the Shopper division, resulting in an adjusted operating profit margin of 14% (FY25: 16%). Excluding the impact of the substantial investment within Shopper, the adjusted operating profit margin for the Group was in line with the prior year at 16%. However, the annual results hide a year of two halves. H1 delivered £24m, down 20% YoY although H2 delivered £30.3m, flat YoY and up 26% on H1. This trend is due to revenue momentum and execution of the VDP.

The Group’s results were impacted by the net appreciation of UK Sterling, as its average exchange rate was 1% higher against the Euro in this period against the prior period. Movement against the US Dollar was 1% lower compared to 31 July 2025. The net impact of foreign exchange on the Group’s adjusted operating profit1 was a decrease of £0.8m compared to the calculation in constant currency terms.

Update on Value Delivery Plan

As announced earlier this year, the Company has launched a VDP which comprises three waves. The waves combine efficiency improvements and enhanced ways of working along with significant transformation enabled by AI. Plus, wave 3 also includes new revenue streams. 

Wave 1, completed in March 2026, delivered an annualised £2.5m reduction in the cost base through targeted headcount and other cost reductions in non-revenue-generating areas. H2 26 includes some benefit for this action already. FY27 will benefit from the full year impact. 

Wave 2 is deep in the detailed planning and implementation phase. It includes a broad range of initiatives. The combined impact of the first two waves is expected to deliver an annualised adjusted operating profit margin uplift of 350bps over the margin achieved in H1 FY26 (12.3%). We have high levels of conviction this target will be achieved prior to the end of FY27.

Wave 3 will focus on opening up new revenue streams through development of AI-powered products and our Data-as-a-Product capabilities. Our product development, data science and technology teams continue to make strides on these initiatives, including introducing imputation to our dataset and developing newer products such as YouGov Parallax.

Strong performance in the financial services sector was driven by the expansion of existing client relationships, while continued momentum with technology clients also contributed to growth. Going concern

These financial statements have been prepared under a going concern basis of accounting. In considering the ability of the Group to continue in operation as a going concern, Management has modelled multiple scenarios, incorporating differing levels of trading performance, and differing macro-economic environments. Management considered cash flows over the period to 31 January 2028, under a base case, severe-but-plausible scenario, and reverse stress test.

The severe-but-plausible scenario modelled a significant revenue downside in comparison with the 2027 budget, accompanied by easily-achievable cost mitigations. This scenario is not a forecast, but is designed to stress test liquidity and covenant compliance.

The reverse stress test modelled a severe revenue downside in comparison with the 2027 budget, designed to cause a breach in covenants. This scenario is deemed implausible, but, if it were to occur, there are further mitigations (above and beyond those taken into account in the severe-but-plausible scenario) that could be applied.

The final repayment date of the Group’s loan facilities is 30 April 2028, which is beyond the going concern period. Management is confident that it will be able to repay these facilities, either through strategic disposals or refinancing. During the year, it agreed two modifications with its syndicate of banks, amending the amounts of the Group’s repayments, and extending the final repayment date. The banks remain supportive of the Group’s plans. As a result, Management does not believe that the facility expiry creates a material uncertainty around the Group’s going concern status.

In performing the above exercise, Management has established that there are no plausible scenarios that would result in the Group no longer being able to continue in operation as a going concern. It has concluded that the Group has adequate resources to continue operating for at least the next year, that it is appropriate to continue to adopt a going concern basis of accounting in preparing the financial statements, and that there is not a material uncertainty in relation to going concern.

Impairment assessment

Goodwill is assessed for impairment at 30 April each year using a value-in-use approach for all CGUs except Shopper, where fair value less costs of disposal is used. The value in use of each CGU has been calculated by discounting their forecasted cash flows. The Group has prepared detailed like-for-like forecasts for the next year, and extrapolated these over five years. It has then applied terminal growth rates and pre-tax discount rates which reflect current market assessments of the time value of money and risks specific to the forecasted cash flows.

The key assumptions used in the value-in-use calculations are revenue growth rates, terminal growth rates, and pre-tax discount rates. In determining revenue growth rates, the Group uses internal and external sources of information, in terminal growth rates industrial and general economic long-term growth rates, and in pre-tax discount rates, established market practices, including risk-free rates, market risk premia and costs of debt.

On 29 September 2023, the Group entered into a secured facilities agreement for four years with a syndicate of banks, led by Citibank, to finance the business combination of Shopper, and to provide working capital headroom. The facilities comprise a €240.0m term loan and €40.0m multi-currency revolving credit facility. Interest is payable quarterly on both facilities at a base rate plus a margin which is dependent on leverage. The base rate on the term loan is EURIBOR, and on the revolving credit facility is dependent on the currency borrowed. Capital repayments are due annually on the term loan.

Both facilities are subject to financial covenants, assessed biannually. Interest cover must not be less than 4:1, and leverage must not be more than 3:1.

On 8 August 2024, the Group purchased a collar to restrict EURIBOR on the term loan. Hedge accounting has not been applied, and all hedge-related income and expenses are recognised within finance income and finance costs in the income statement.

On 11 August 2025, the Group agreed a modification to the term loan, amending the amounts of the annual capital repayments to €20.0m, and of the final balance payable on 29 September 2027 to €164.0m.

On 18 July 2026, the Group agreed a second modification to the term loan, extending the date of the final balance payable to 30 April 2028, and introducing an additional €20.0m capital repayment on 31 October 2027.

At 31 July 2026, £16.7m and €14.0m were drawn down on the revolving credit facility, with €184.0m of the term loan outstanding.
